entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2.  This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant to direct the Judicial Magistrate (Junior Division)/FTC-2, Farrukhabad to add the Section 376 IPC against the opposite party no. 2 along with Sections 498A, 323, 506 IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, arising out of Case Crime No. 399 of 2022 in Criminal Case No. 319 of 2022 (State vs. Kunal alias Chunnu).
3.

Counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has filed the instant application with a prayer that Judicial Magistrate (J.D.)/F.T.C., Farrukhabad be directed to add Section 376 IPC along with Khushbu Verma vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53793288/
1 Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506 IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act against the opposite party no. 2.

entities.text: Khushbu Verma vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He next submits that, prima facie, from the evidences collected during investigation by the Investigating Officer offence under Section 376 IPC is made out against the opposite party no. 2 but learned Magistrate has not summoned the opposite party no. 2 under Section 376 IPC.

He next submits that earlier applicant's father challenged the summoning order before this Court by filing Criminal Revision No. 509 of 2023 and this Court vide order dated 08.02.2023 rejected the same.
4. Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposes the submissions raised by counsel for the applicant.

5. Considered the submissions raised by counsel for the parties and perused the entire record.
6.After investigation, Investigating Officer has submitted charge-sheet under Sections 498-A, 323,
504, 506 IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act against opposite party no. 2 as he has not found any offence under Section 376 IPC.
On perusal of record and perusal of statements of mother and other witnesses, only corroborates the allegations of demand of dowry.
Moreover, the applicant has remedy to raise this objection of at the time of framing of charge before trial court.
As such, no interference is warranted by this Court at this stage.
7. The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
